issues.legal_issue: A statutory power to reopen final agricultural ceiling determinations on specified grounds does not violate the basic structure or improperly displace judicial power when its exercise is subject to judicial review.
material_facts: The ceiling authorities had determined the appellants’ ceiling areas, and the appellants maintained that those determinations had become final.

The State Government directed the cases to be reopened and decided afresh under a provision permitting reopening of final orders made contrary to the Act when prejudicial to the State’s interests or affected by newly discovered important matter or evidence.
The appellants challenged the provision as conferring arbitrary executive power to nullify judicial decisions.
issues.conclusion: The reopening provision is constitutional: it confers a limited power based on specified grounds, and an order reopening a case is subject to judicial scrutiny.
issues.legal_principle: The Rajasthan Imposition of Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1973, Section 15, permits reopening only on the grounds specified in that section. An order not founded on those relevant considerations is liable to be struck down by a court. The provision therefore does not alter the Constitution’s basic structure or encroach upon judicial power.

predicates.ceiling_case_reopening_challenge: The proceeding challenges a power to reopen a final determination in an agricultural land-ceiling case.
predicates.reopening_limited_to_statutory_grounds: The law permits reopening only when the final determination contravenes the law and specified grounds, such as prejudice to the State’s interests or newly discovered important matter or evidence, are present.
predicates.reopening_order_subject_to_judicial_revi: A court may review whether an order reopening the case rests on the grounds specified by law.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns reopening a final agricultural ceiling determination, and reopening is confined to specified grounds and reviewable by a court, the limited reopening power is constitutional.

issues.legal_issue: A land-ceiling law enacted within the legislature’s authority over land and protected as an agrarian-reform measure cannot be invalidated on the asserted grounds of legislative incompetence or violation of fundamental rights.
material_facts: The appellants challenged the validity of the provision authorizing reopening of agricultural ceiling cases.
The law concerned ceilings on agricultural land and was enacted to implement agrarian reform.
The Act was included in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.
issues.conclusion: The State Legislature was competent to enact the land-ceiling law, and the Act was protected from challenge on the ground that it violated fundamental rights.
issues.legal_principle: Entry 18 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule gives the State Legislature competence to legislate on land. The Court held that agrarian-reform legislation of this kind was protected under Articles 31-A and 31-C and, because the Act was placed in the Ninth Schedule, was immune from challenge on the ground of violation of fundamental rights. It also relied on Sukhdarshan Singh v. State of Rajasthan, in which Section 15 had been upheld.

rule.if: land_ceiling_law_challenge and legislature_has_authority_over_land and law_implements_agrarian_reform and act_has_fundamental_rights_protection

predicates.land_ceiling_law_challenge: The proceeding challenges a law governing ceilings on agricultural land.
predicates.legislature_has_authority_over_land: The legislature enacting the law has authority to legislate on land.
predicates.law_implements_agrarian_reform: The law is directed to implementing agrarian reform.
predicates.act_has_fundamental_rights_protection: The law has constitutional protection against a challenge based on violation of fundamental rights.

issues.definition: When a land-ceiling law is challenged, the enacting legislature has authority over land, the law implements agrarian reform, and the law has fundamental-rights protection, the challenge based on legislative competence and fundamental rights fails.
